elsa: Following up on the hosted/dedicated/private surface discussion 1: propose we add a very small discovery handshake so Private can run without a sidecar by default. Key goals: minimal latency, clear auth hints, a graceful legacy fallback.

ravi: Can you outline the handshake state machine at a high level? I'm worried about complexity creeping into routing.

elsa: Super small: (1) controlplane validates client token; (2) controlplane probes runtime on first contact for tenant -> POST /_redwood/discover; (3) runtime replies with a compact manifest (capabilities + auth_hint + optional ttl); (4) controlplane caches manifest per-tenant and routes accordingly. If probe fails we route to a legacy adapter.

gwen: Important: controlplane must never be a key-holder. Runtime should provide an attestation blob and mTLS identity; controlplane validates attest and uses references, not keys.

ravi: How long do we cache manifests? Tradeoff between probe load and staleness.

elsa: Default 300s. Runtime can request a shorter cap_ttl_seconds (min 30s) or longer (max 3600s). We'll enforce bounds. Also support a runtime webhook to invalidate cache immediately on rotation.

gwen: For legacy installs without the endpoint, what's the UX? We should surface that clearly to customers.

elsa: Fallback path: mark tenant as "legacy_adapter" in the cache, increment metric legacy_adapter_routes, and show a console banner recommending runtime upgrade. Also add an audit event when we create the mapping.

ravi: Metrics/alerts we need: discovery_latency_ms, discovery_error_rate, legacy_adapter_rate. Circuit breaker: if discovery_error_rate > 2% for 5m, temporarily move new tenants to legacy_adapter and page infra.

gwen: Also track attestation validation failures separately (security will want 90/99 breakdowns). Record attestation_ttl and runtime_cert_subject in audit logs.

elsa: Agreed. Plan to require client cert validation and to log cert fingerprint and tenant id for audits.

ravi: Sample manifest shape so on-prem teams can implement quickly? Keep it tiny.

elsa: Example payload we'll publish in the runtime README:

```
# POST /_redwood/discover
Request: {"probe_version":"1","controlplane_id":"us-east-1-cp-42"}
Response 200: {"tenant_id":"acme","capabilities":["kvcache","batch_infer"],"auth_hint":"attestation+mTLS","preferred_variants":["q4_0","q8_0"],"cap_ttl_seconds":300}
```

gwen: Include preferred_variants so routing can pick cheaper variants in Dedicated vs Private. Make max_seq_len advisory only.

ravi: Testing and rollout? We want to minimize customer risk.

elsa: Rollout plan: feature-flag private_handshake_v2; unit tests for parsing + cache behavior; integration test against a local probe server; Dedicated canary (48h); opt-in Private tenants; broad enable when discovery_error_rate < 0.5% and legacy_adapter_rate < 1% over 1h.

gwen: Ops: add dashboards for discovery_* metrics and legacy_adapter_rate. Billing note: legacy adapter incurs extra CPU; expose legacy_adapter_routed_requests to finance.

infra-robot: action: add feature-flag private_handshake_v2, create metrics discovery_latency_ms, discovery_error_rate, legacy_adapter_rate, and alert if legacy_adapter_rate > 1% over 5m.

sec-team: Please ensure the RFC notes the attestation validation steps and retention requirements for audit events.

elsa: Will draft the follow-up RFC with the explicit state machine, probe schema, cache TTL policy, and rollout checklist. Who wants the integration pairing?

ravi: I'll pair on integration tests.

gwen: I'll take the runtime README and console copy.

elsa: Thanks everyone 1 I'll post the RFC draft and add the feature-flag to the feature board. :shipit:
